**Abolitionists Rising.** Their stated goals are "the abolition of abortion, the repentance of the nation, and the glorification of God." Their marks: immediate and not gradual, equal protection, no exceptions, biblical and not secular, and obeying God over unjust rulings. (abolitionistsrising.com)
Then give [The Gospel](/topic/the-gospel).

topics.title: MacArthur on Rome

intro.text: These lines come from John MacArthur's sermons on the Pope and the papacy, the Mass, the priesthood, Galatians 5 and the idolatry of Mary worship (Grace to You). Use them to know where our teachers stand and why. With a Catholic friend, open the Bible first and ask questions; these are for your own conviction and for when someone asks, "Is it really that serious?"

lines.text: He begins with grief, not anger: "We find no delight in people who are condemned to hell." And he ends with a plea: "People need to be rescued from this system." (Ezek 33:11; Rom 10:1; 2 Tim 2:24–26)

MacArthur calls Roman Catholicism "an apostate, corrupt, heretical, false Christianity" and "a front for the kingdom of Satan." On adding works to faith he says, "There is no room for any alteration of the gospel." Of Rome and Eastern Orthodoxy together: "It is not to be joined, it is to be cursed." He is using Paul's word, anathema. (Gal 1:6–9; Gal 5:2–4; 2 Cor 11:13–15; 2 Pet 2:1)

lines.label: Backing
lines.text: Trent placed its curse on justification by faith alone [Sess. 6, can. 9, 12, 14] and has never withdrawn it. Paul put his curse on any gospel that adds to faith.

He calls transubstantiation "mystical hocus-pocus, mumbo-jumbo for sure," and says that phrase came from the Latin words of the Mass, *hoc est corpus meum*. He says the Mass is paid for: "You pay for a Mass. That's how the coffers of the Catholic Church are filled." And he reminds us that English believers were burned alive for denying it. (Heb 9:25–28; Heb 10:10–14; Heb 10:18)

lines.label: Backing
lines.text: Rome's own law lets a priest accept an offering to apply a Mass for a named intention [Code of Canon Law, can. 945]. Trent calls the Mass propitiatory for the living and the dead [Sess. 22, can. 3].

lines.text: The New Testament survives in thousands of Greek manuscripts, some copied within a few generations of the originals. The writers were eyewitnesses or wrote down what eyewitnesses told them, while many witnesses were still alive to object. (Luke 1:1–4; 2 Pet 1:16; 1 John 1:1–3; 1 Cor 15:3–8)

topics.title: Words they use

lines.label: Jehovah
lines.text: their preferred form of God's name (YHWH). For them it names the Father only.

lines.label: New World Translation (NWT)
lines.text: the Watchtower's own Bible translation.

lines.label: Watchtower / Governing Body
lines.text: the leadership that directs all Witness teaching and calls itself the "faithful and discreet slave."

lines.label: Active force
lines.text: their term for the Holy Spirit, whom they say is not a person.

lines.label: Kingdom Interlinear
lines.text: the Watchtower's own Greek and English New Testament. Useful because it prints the Greek with a word-for-word English line next to their NWT.

lines.label: The 144,000
lines.text: the "anointed" who they say go to heaven. Everyone else hopes for life on a paradise earth.

lines.label: Biblical Unitarian
lines.text: holds that God is one person, the Father, and Jesus is a human Messiah.

lines.label: Arian
lines.text: holds that the Son is God's first and greatest creature.

lines.label: Shaliach (agency)
lines.text: the Jewish idea that a sent agent stands for the one who sent him. They use it to explain away texts where Jesus speaks as God.

lines.label: Oneness / modalism
lines.text: God is one Person who shows Himself as Father, Son and Spirit (as roles or modes, not three Persons). Oneness Pentecostals say that one Person is Jesus.

lines.label: Homoousios
lines.text: "of the same essence," the Nicene term for the Son's relation to the Father.

lines.label: Malak / angelos
lines.text: Hebrew and Greek for "messenger." It names a job, not a nature.

lines.label: Godhead
lines.text: for them, three separate beings who are one in purpose.

lines.label: Exaltation
lines.text: the teaching that faithful people can become gods.

lines.label: Great Apostasy
lines.text: their claim that the true church was lost after the apostles.

lines.label: Restoration
lines.text: their claim that Joseph Smith restored the church.

lines.label: Standard works
lines.text: their four books of scripture: the Bible, the Book of Mormon, the Doctrine and Covenants (D&C), and the Pearl of Great Price.

lines.label: JST
lines.text: the Joseph Smith Translation, his revision of the Bible.

lines.label: Testimony / burning in the bosom
lines.text: an inner feeling taken as God's confirmation that the church is true.

lines.label: King Follett discourse
lines.text: Joseph Smith's 1844 sermon teaching that God was once a man.

lines.label: Tawhid
lines.text: the absolute oneness of Allah.

lines.label: Shirk
lines.text: associating anything with Allah. The one sin Allah will not forgive if a person dies in it (Q 4:48).

lines.label: Isa
lines.text: the Quran's name for Jesus.

lines.label: Tawrat, Zabur, Injil
lines.text: the Torah, the Psalms and the Gospel, which the Quran says Allah revealed.

lines.label: Tahrif
lines.text: the claim that the earlier Scriptures were corrupted.

lines.label: Hadith
lines.text: reports of what Muhammad said and did.

lines.label: Surah / ayah
lines.text: a chapter and a verse of the Quran.

lines.label: Tafsir
lines.text: commentary on the Quran.

lines.label: Hafs, Warsh, Qalun
lines.text: different transmitted readings of the Quran.

lines.label: Magisterium
lines.text: the Church's teaching office (the pope and the bishops in communion with him), which alone can authentically interpret Scripture and Tradition [CCC 85, 100].

lines.label: Sacred Tradition
lines.text: teaching handed down outside Scripture and held with "equal" reverence [CCC 82].

lines.label: Ex cathedra
lines.text: the pope defining faith or morals "from the chair," held to be infallible and "irreformable" [Vatican I].

lines.label: Transubstantiation
lines.text: the whole substance of bread and wine becomes Christ's body and blood, "truly, really, and substantially" [Trent, Sess. 13, can. 1; CCC 1376].

lines.label: Latria / dulia / hyperdulia
lines.text: worship due to God alone / honor to saints / the higher honor given to Mary.

lines.label: Infused vs. imputed righteousness
lines.text: Rome says God makes us "inwardly just" [CCC 1992]. Scripture says God credits Christ's righteousness to us (Rom 4:6; 2 Cor 5:21).

lines.label: Mortal sin
lines.text: grave sin that destroys sanctifying grace and, if unrepented, leads to hell [CCC 1861].

lines.label: Purgatory
lines.text: final purification after death for those who die in grace "but still imperfectly purified" [CCC 1030–1031].

lines.label: Indulgence
lines.text: remission of temporal punishment for sins already forgiven, applicable to oneself or to souls in purgatory [CCC 1471, 1498].

lines.label: Deuterocanonical books
lines.text: what Rome calls the Apocrypha: Tobit, Judith, Wisdom, Sirach, Baruch, 1–2 Maccabees, and additions to Esther and Daniel [Trent, Sess. 4].

lines.label: Judaizers
lines.text: teachers in the New Testament who believed in Jesus and said Gentiles must also be circumcised and keep the Law of Moses to be saved (Acts 15:1, 5). Galatians was written against them.

lines.label: Necessary vs. sufficient
lines.text: Rome says grace, faith and Scripture are necessary. The Reformation said each is also enough: Scripture alone, grace alone, faith alone, Christ alone.

lines.label: Unam Sanctam
lines.text: the 1302 bull of Boniface VIII that defined submission to the Roman Pontiff as necessary for salvation.

lines.label: Holy Tradition
lines.text: "the doctrine of the faith, the law of God, the sacraments, and the ritual as handed down" [Philaret Q17]. It includes Scripture and the councils.

lines.label: Theosis (deification)
lines.text: sharing in the life of God as the goal of salvation [GOARCH, "Spirituality"]. Not sharing God's essence.

lines.label: Synergy
lines.text: God's grace and human effort working together in salvation.

lines.label: Theotokos
lines.text: "God-bearer," the title for Mary affirmed at Ephesus (431).

lines.label: Ever-virgin
lines.text: Mary remained a virgin before, during and after Christ's birth [Philaret Q186].

lines.label: Proskynesis vs. latreia
lines.text: veneration (bowing, kissing) given to icons and saints / worship given to God alone [Nicaea II].

lines.label: Ancestral sin
lines.text: we inherit death and corruption from Adam, but not his guilt [OCA Q&A, "Original Sin"].

lines.label: Essence / energies
lines.text: God's unknowable essence vs. His uncreated energies, in which believers participate (Gregory Palamas).

lines.label: Toll houses
lines.text: a pious tradition about demonic testing of the soul after death; **not dogma**.

lines.label: Dormition
lines.text: Mary's "falling asleep" (Aug. 15). Many Orthodox believe she was taken bodily to heaven, but the East never defined it as Rome did in 1950.

lines.label: Chrismation
lines.text: anointing with holy oil (chrism) right after baptism, the Orthodox form of confirmation. It is also how most converts from other churches are received.

lines.label: Infant communion
lines.text: baptized and chrismated infants receive communion [OCA, *The Orthodox Faith*, vol. 2].

lines.label: Prayers for the departed
lines.text: prayers, alms and the liturgy offered for the dead, which Dositheus says deliver some souls from Hades [Decree 18].

lines.label: Atheist
lines.text: does not believe in God. Some go further and say there is no God.

lines.label: Agnostic
lines.text: says they don't know, or that no one can know.

lines.label: Naturalism
lines.text: the view that nature is all there is.

lines.label: Objective morality
lines.text: right and wrong that are true whatever anyone thinks.

lines.label: Burden of proof
lines.text: whoever makes a claim has to back it up. "There is no God" is a claim.

lines.label: Trinity
lines.text: one God in three Persons. See [The Trinity](/topic/the-trinity).

lines.label: Two natures
lines.text: Jesus is one Person who is truly God and truly man.

lines.label: Ransom
lines.text: the price that frees a captive. Scripture says no man can pay it for another and that God redeems. Jesus gave His life as the ransom.

lines.label: Mediator
lines.text: the one who stands between God and men. Jesus is the one mediator because He is truly God and truly man.

lines.label: Monogenes
lines.text: the unique, only begotten Son. It marks His unique, eternal relationship to the Father, never creation (LSB: "only begotten").

lines.label: Prototokos
lines.text: Greek for "firstborn." In texts like Col 1:15 (cf. Ps 89:27) it means the preeminent heir, not the first one created.

lines.label: Arche
lines.text: Greek for "beginning," "origin" or "ruler."
